brief.summary: Equity futures slipped about 0.2-0.4% while the front end stayed elevated after an ~11bp Friday repricing on Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech; 2s sit near 4.32%, 30s around 5.20-5.26%, and the curve is modestly steeper. Markets price roughly 60% odds of a September hike and about 40bp through year-end, though most guests expect a hold. Brent jumped above $91 on renewed US-Iran strikes and Hormuz mining, feeding commodity inflation, while gold pushed higher and the dollar slid, notably against the yen. Nvidia's strong outlook and $3.5bn MediaTek investment kept the AI capex story alive, but guests flagged a high earnings bar and emerging consumer fatigue. Tone was cautiously risk-off.
notable_quotes: Is this a Fed that's actually credible in delivering tightening, or is this, as they say out west, all hat and no cattle?
We want to make clear today that no one is above the reach of U.S. sanctions.
